limitations: Official historical 2022 and 2024 results are compared with a frozen unofficial 2026 reported-count observation, not an estimate of final turnout or counting completeness.
Counts are ballot observations, not House candidate votes. The separately reviewed 2026 House candidate total is 234595, not the 239057 ballot count used here.
Every selected native precinct ballot row is included. Each year reconciles precincts to all 53 counties and the native statewide control.
Historical county totals are derived precinct sums, not independently supplied county controls.
County names match exactly, without fuzzy aliases or geographic allocation. This is not a fixed-person cohort or analytical boundary-overlay certification.
Historical county identifiers are legacy portal ordinals, not FIPS. Current identifiers are separate native location IDs; precinct IDs need only be unique within their own current county.

The 398 historical 2022, 385 historical 2024 and 358 current reporting units are not a qualified longitudinal precinct panel. Existing Morton and Towner mapping caveats remain; no map or analytical crosswalk is added.

Native historical Eligible Voters means estimated residents aged 18 or older, not registered voters, voting-eligible population or a fixed eligible cohort. Those native denominators remain in the selected facts but are not used to calculate rates.
Historical native source clocks have no supplied timezone. Acquisition times, HTTP Last-Modified, source clocks and the current UTC revision are distinct provenance fields.
No individual dropoff, returning or newly eligible identity, party switching, demographic turnout rate or causal persuasion is identified by these counts.

Offline reproduction starts with the complete selected ballot facts. Re-running initial native extraction separately requires the pinned original sources; copyrighted site markup and unrelated contests are not mirrored or relicensed.
This analysis is not endorsed by the North Dakota Secretary of State and does not close the missing North Dakota joint-choice survey or individual-transition evidence gap.
